exposure: Placental Abruption (leading to urgent caesarean delivery)
outcome: FOXP3-positive cell infiltration in placental chorionic villi
FOXP3-positive cell infiltration in placental bed (cumulative)
cohort: The study included 13 patients with placenta accreta syndrome and a control group of 66 women who had caesarean deliveries, comprising 44 with elective caesarean delivery and 22 with urgent caesarean delivery due to placental abruption.
finding: FOXP3-positive cell infiltration in chorionic villi was significantly different between studied groups, being most commonly observed in placenta accreta syndrome patients and least frequently in patients after urgent caesarean delivery due to placental abruption.
mod_finding: FOXP3-positive cell infiltration in chorionic villi was least frequently presented in patients after urgent caesarean delivery (5%) compared to those after elective caesarean delivery (18%).
cross-section timing: At the time of caesarean delivery
